source: d'Aliberti & Ribeiro (2026) The Illusion of Insight in Reasoning Models
finding: Mid-trace 'Wait, let's reconsider' shifts in GRPO-tuned Qwen2.5 and Llama models are rare and go with lower accuracy, so they do not look like Gestalt insight.
numbers: 1M+ traces, 3 domains (cryptic crosswords, MATH-500, Rush Hour). Shifts in 6.31% of traces pooled (about 7.6% for Qwen2.5-1.5B). Accuracy 2.57% with a shift vs 16.44% without, N=723,200.
limits: Shift detector is lexical plus judge based; authors checked formal, GPT-based and lexical variants and all agree. Small base models (1.5B) carry most of the data.
agent_relevance: Do not treat a spontaneous 'wait' in a trace as evidence of restructuring. Do not count it as progress.

source: d'Aliberti & Ribeiro (2026) The Illusion of Insight in Reasoning Models - formal Aha definition
finding: A strict 'Aha' (prior failures, prior stability, and a gain at the pivot) almost never occurs.
numbers: Formal detector fires on only 1.79% of samples pooled over Crossword/Math/RHour checkpoints and temperatures. Even with lax thresholds the share of problem-checkpoint pairs is only about 0.6% to 3% for Qwen2.5-1.5B at T=0.7.
limits: Defined on problem-checkpoint pairs during RL training; says nothing about a single-pass agent loop.
agent_relevance: Gives a usable operational test for real restructuring: the same item failed before and now succeeds because of a strategy change.

source: d'Aliberti & Ribeiro (2026) The Illusion of Insight in Reasoning Models - external models
finding: The same low base rate and no accuracy benefit show up in DeepSeek-R1 and GPT-4o on MATH-500.
numbers: Canonical shifts: DeepSeek-R1 0.00-0.25% of traces, GPT-4o 0.88-2.21% across T in {0,0.05,0.3,0.7,1}. For GPT-4o accuracy given a shift is below accuracy without a shift at every temperature. R1 shift counts are tiny so estimates are unstable.
limits: Only MATH-500 for the external models; R1 counts too small to judge.
agent_relevance: Frontier reasoning models also do not show restructuring in the Gestalt sense on maths.

source: d'Aliberti & Ribeiro (2026) The Illusion of Insight in Reasoning Models - entropy and training stage
finding: Spontaneous shifts do not become helpful later in training or when the model is uncertain. The effect depends on temperature (sometimes helpful at low T, like noise at high T).
numbers: Pooled shift-vs-entropy odds ratio 0.77 (95% CI 0.58-1.02, p=0.070, N=723,200). Math: shifts harmful even in high-entropy traces (-7.40 pp) and more so in low entropy (-22.88 pp). Xwords high-entropy +0.63 pp, noisy. RHour accuracy near zero. Math training-step AME -0.0615 (p=1.55e-4).
limits: Associations, not causal. Entropy gate uses the top 20% of pass-1 sequence entropy per domain.
agent_relevance: A shift is a symptom of unstable inference. Use entropy as the trigger, not the shift itself.

source: d'Aliberti & Ribeiro (2026) The Illusion of Insight in Reasoning Models - forced Aha intervention
finding: Forcing a second pass with a reconsideration cue ('Wait, we need to reconsider. Let's think this through step by step.') helps, most of all on math.
numbers: Pass 2 vs Pass 1: MATH-500 32.2% to 40.6% (+8.41 pp; 50,574 wrong-to-right vs 23,500 right-to-wrong); crosswords +0.45 pp (9.70% to 10.15%); Rush Hour +0.01 pp (near-zero base). Reported overall and under a high-entropy gate.
limits: Second generation costs extra compute, so compute is not matched. Paired counts show 23,500 regressions too. Small GRPO-tuned models.
agent_relevance: Direct template for a restructuring operator: detect high uncertainty, then force a fresh look. Budget for regressions.

source: d'Aliberti & Ribeiro (2026) The Illusion of Insight in Reasoning Models - detector variants and cue wording
finding: Conclusions held across three detector types and across reconsideration cue wordings.
numbers: Detectors: formal, GPT-based, lexical, all same direction. Three semantically similar cues (C1-C3) tested in App. C.4. The paper cites earlier work reporting up to 30% of hesitations misread as insight in some settings.
limits: Per-cue gains are in the appendix and were not read in full.
agent_relevance: Trigger text can be swapped; the entropy gate matters more than the wording.

source: Mizumoto et al. (2025) The Metacognitive Bottleneck: Japanese Riddles (NazoNazo Benchmark)
finding: Japanese riddles that need representational restructuring (puns, character decomposition) are hard for most LLMs. The best model (GPT-5) falls inside the human confidence interval.
numbers: 201 riddles; human reference on a 120-item subset n=126, mean 52.9% (95% CI 46.6-59.2%), bimodal score distribution (peaks at 0 and 20 of 20). 38 LLMs zero-shot, no retrieval: non-reasoning avg 7.6%, reasoning avg 17.6% on the subset. Full 201 items: 9.42% vs 19.25%, OR 2.29 (95% CI 1.99-2.64).
limits: Parameter count did not predict accuracy, release date did. No formal model-by-human test. Public riddles, so contamination is possible. Single research group.
agent_relevance: Insight-type items are a useful hold-out test of restructuring that scale alone does not fix.

source: Mizumoto et al. (2025) Metacognitive Bottleneck - verification failure
finding: Models often write the right answer in their thought log and then do not commit to it ('verification failure').
numbers: Share of incorrect answers where a gold variant appears in the thought log: DeepSeek-R1-0528 30.57% (48 of 199 answered), Claude Opus 4 25.00%, Grok 4 39.34%, Gemini 2.5 Flash Preview 5.23%. Range 5% to 39%.
limits: Counted by literal string match, so it can overcount. Logs may be unfaithful. Only 4 models had usable logs.
agent_relevance: Candidate generation is not the bottleneck; recognising 'that is it' is. Add an endorse-or-reject step and scan the trace for earlier candidates before the final answer.

source: Mizumoto et al. (2025) Metacognitive Bottleneck - language and false insight
finding: Which language the model thinks in did not reliably help. Models also show 'false insight', confident commitment to a wrong reframing.
numbers: Grok 4: 29.5% (33/112) thinking in Japanese vs 48.8% (40/82) in English, p=0.0071. DeepSeek-R1-0528 23.1% (46/199), all Japanese. Claude Opus 4 36.7% (16/44) vs 28.7% (45/157), p=0.356. Gemini 2.5 Flash 0/12 vs 22/188, p=0.369.
limits: Only one of four models shows a significant language effect. Thought-log language is self-selected, not randomised. False insight is described qualitatively, not counted.
agent_relevance: Two failure types need two fixes: missed restructuring (generate more frames) and false insight (verify before commit).

source: Mizumoto et al. (2025) Metacognitive Bottleneck - contamination design
finding: The authors propose rotating open, blind and post-cutoff private item sets to keep an insight benchmark clean.
numbers: Open set 42 items, blind set 159 items (includes the 120 human-comparison items), plus new items made after each model's training cutoff.
limits: A proposal, not yet shown to work at scale.
agent_relevance: Our in-house insight test should keep a private set and a reworded twin for each item.

source: Haq et al. (2025) Is your LLM trapped in a Mental Set?
finding: Tests Einstellung-style mental set on LLMs with DeCaro (2016) maths equivalence problems. Chain-of-thought changes accuracy and step count.
numbers: Six complex and six shortcut problems per condition. Few-shot exact match, shortcut alone vs shortcut after complex: GPT-4o 0.33 to 0.66, Llama-3.1-70B 0 to 0.16, Llama-3.1-8B 0.16 to 0. With few-shot plus zero-shot CoT, GPT-4o 0.66/0.66/0.83/0.83 and steps rose to 3 for all models vs 1 without CoT.
limits: n=6 per cell, one run, no variance and no statistics. Authors read the extra steps as mental set induced by CoT. Weak evidence.
agent_relevance: CoT can lock in the long procedure. A restructuring step should ask 'is there a shortcut?' before working step by step.

source: Yang et al. (2025) Understanding Aha Moments: from External Observations to Internal Mechanisms
finding: Compares aha and no-aha R1-style models on Knights and Knaves and Countdown puzzles. Aha models use more human-like words and adjust uncertainty to difficulty.
numbers: Synthetic puzzles with difficulty levels. RASM metric (log odds of anthropomorphic vs reasoning token probability) separates aha from no-aha models. Aha models suppress language mixing and path repetition at difficulty 3-6 (rates near zero). Latent PCA shows difficulty recognised in earlier layers.
limits: Descriptive and correlational, small distilled models. Aha vs no-aha is defined by training recipe, not by a per-item gain test. The Illusion of Insight paper tests that link and finds no accuracy benefit.
agent_relevance: Difficulty-aware uncertainty is a possible trigger signal for re-framing.

source: Liu et al. (2025) Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training: A Critical Perspective
finding: The R1-Zero 'aha moment' is already in base models, so RL did not create it. More self-reflection did not mean higher accuracy.
numbers: DeepSeek-V3-Base-685B already emits 'Aha' and 'wait' style self-reflection on 500 MATH questions with the R1 template. In R1-Zero, self-reflection is more frequent but not positively correlated with accuracy (their Sec F).
limits: Keyword pool kept small to avoid false positives (recheck, rethink, reassess...). Inference-time analysis only; reflection may still help exploration in training.
agent_relevance: Aha words are cheap and already present in pretraining text. They are not proof of restructuring.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) R1-Zero's Aha Moment in Visual Reasoning on a 2B Non-SFT Model
finding: Reports a replication of R1-style self-reflection and longer responses in a 2B vision model with RL alone, after other multimodal attempts failed to show them.
numbers: Qwen2-VL-2B with GRPO on SAT data reaches 59.47% on CV-Bench, about 30% above the base model and about 2% above SFT (their numbers). RL on already fine-tuned visual models did not reproduce the effect.
limits: Work-in-progress report. Aha judged from sampled text, no per-item gain test.
agent_relevance: Surface behaviour replicates only from some starting points. It does not show a function.

source: Wu et al. (2026) Aha Moment Revisited: Are VLMs Truly Capable of Self Verification in Inference-time Scaling?
finding: In RL-trained vision-language models, aha behaviours give no reliable gain and majority voting beats self-verification.
numbers: Aha moments occur in only 8.3% of responses (judged by GPT-4o). Correction rates from wrong first answers are low. Majority vote gains about +4.5% over greedy on GeoQA; best-of-N with self-verification falls up to -16.7% for the VLAA models. Self-verification is sometimes better with the image removed.
limits: Visual maths only (GeoQA, MathVista); five open VLMs.
agent_relevance: Prefer sampling several framings and voting over one model checking itself.

source: Hu et al. (2025) Beyond 'Aha!': Toward Systematic Meta-Abilities Alignment in Large Reasoning Models
finding: Argues aha moments are unpredictable and uncontrollable, so it trains deduction, induction and abduction explicitly instead.
numbers: Three-stage pipeline (individual alignment, parameter merging, domain RL) gives over 10% relative gain over instruction-tuned baselines, and a further gain in ceiling for 7B and 32B on math, code and science.
limits: A training method, not a scaffold. Aha is taken as given, not tested for function.
agent_relevance: Abduction (best explanation for a surprise) is the closest named operation to restructuring. Name the inference type needed at an impasse.

source: Chen & Wang (2026) A Comprehensive Anatomy of Human and DeepSeek-R1 LLM Mathematical Reasoning
finding: Step-level human annotation of 10,247 R1 steps on AIME 2025 calls much of R1 'reflection' topological mimicry.
numbers: 30 problems. Experienced human spends about 15% of steps on framing and planning; R1 spends roughly 40% in analysis-type steps with shallow verification loops. Failed traces either barely use or overuse branch and backtrace. Reflection helps only when placed inside deductive inference.
limits: One model (DeepSeek-R1-0120), one human reference solver, one contest. Proposals (backtrace-depth filter, threshold 0.1) are not validated.
agent_relevance: Penalise spinning-wheel verification loops. Spend retries on re-framing (branch and backtrack), not on re-checking arithmetic.

source: Chen et al. (2025) EvolMathEval: Evolvable Benchmarks for Mathematical Reasoning
finding: Names a 'Pseudo Aha Moment' failure: the model grabs a flawed shortcut instead of multi-step reasoning on mutated problems.
numbers: On problems built by approximate substitution, the pseudo-aha pattern was responsible for 77% to 100% of incorrect answers depending on model.
limits: Problems were evolved to trap models, so the rate is for an adversarial set.
agent_relevance: Machine form of false insight (Danek and Wiley): a confident wrong shortcut. Check any shortcut against the original constraints before commit.

source: Jiang et al. (2023) BRAINTEASER: Lateral Thinking Puzzles for Large Language Models
finding: First lateral-thinking benchmark (1,100 puzzles). Models are near random on hard cases and break down on reworded versions.
numbers: Best model ChatGPT 53% (word puzzles) and 63% (sentence puzzles) vs human 92% and random 25%. About a third of models at or below random. ChatGPT failed 45% of original puzzles whose context-reconstructed twin it solved; RoBERTa-L 61%. Commonsense-knowledge adaptation hurt sentence puzzles. Number of few-shot demos had no clear effect on sentence puzzles.
limits: 2023 models only.
agent_relevance: Default commonsense association is the fixation to overcome; more commonsense training makes it worse. Use reconstruction twins to separate restructuring from recall.

source: Jiang et al. (2023) BRAINTEASER - memorisation error analysis
finding: Models recall the riddle without the reasoning path.
numbers: ChatGPT began its answer to 'How do you spell COW in thirteen letters?' with 'The question seems to be a brain teaser'. It scored best on original word puzzles, unlike every other case, which the authors link to memorisation. Humans lose little on the group metric; all models lose much.
limits: Qualitative examples, not counts.
agent_relevance: Recall of riddles passes for insight in a one-shot test. Use unseen, reworded twins.

source: Chen et al. (2024) Weak-eval-Strong: SPLAT situation puzzles
finding: Situation puzzles with a yes/no player-judge protocol (975 puzzles, 3 levels). Using the benchmark's reasoning process as prompts raises scores on other lateral tasks.
numbers: Judge agreement with humans over 80%. RiddleSense dev accuracy with their reasoning prompts: Llama3-8B 70.51 to 72.18, Llama3-70B 83.34 to 85.21, GPT-4 88.83 to 89.23. With their data: Llama3-8B 61.45 to 64.07, Llama3-70B 80.76 to 83.78 on average.
limits: Gains are small (0.4 to 3 points). The judge is itself an LLM (WizardLM-2).
agent_relevance: Interactive yes/no probing of a hidden frame is a ready-made operator: ask questions that split the frame space.

source: Ismayilzada et al. (2026) CresOWLve: Benchmarking Creative Problem-Solving Over Real-World Knowledge
finding: 2,061 expert quiz puzzles need a non-obvious link between facts. Models know the facts but miss the leap.
numbers: Non-thinking models all under 30% (GPT-4.1 best). GPT-5.4 nearly doubles from no thinking to medium effort. Strongest thinking models lose over 20 points from Very Simple to Very Hard. Creative vs factual questions: drop of 6.08 points (Gemini-3.1-Pro high) to 17.21 points (Mistral-Large-3). Top errors: missing creative connection and clue misinterpretation. Difficulty did not track number of domains, semantic distance or atomic facts.
limits: Public quiz material, so contamination possible. Russian version scored higher for thinking models (up to +15 LLM-judge), partly flagged as contamination.
agent_relevance: Failures are not missing knowledge but missing the connecting frame. More thinking effort is a clear lever; diversify frames.

source: Lee et al. (2025) Puzzled by Puzzles: When Vision-Language Models Can't Take a Hint
finding: 432 hand-made rebus puzzles. VLMs fail on lateral and abstract cases. Closed reasoning models do far better than non-reasoning ones.
numbers: Naive-match accuracy: GPT-5 60.42%, o3 54.56%, o4-mini 48.16%, gemini-2.5-pro 39.99%, gpt-4o 18.75%; small open models about 0.5% to 10%. Human non-expert and expert rows are garbled in the PDF text (expert about 76-81%), so treat as approximate.
limits: English puzzles only. Table extraction was messy.
agent_relevance: Same pattern as text insight tasks: reasoning models help, small ones do not; experts still ahead.

source: Loewe et al. (2024) Abrupt and spontaneous strategy switches emerge in simple regularised neural networks
finding: Sudden, delayed, selective insight-like switches appear in plain gradient-trained networks with L1-regularised gating and noisy updates. No special insight module is needed.
numbers: 99 humans and 99 networks on a hidden-colour task. Humans: 49/99 (49.5%) steeper than the control maximum; 79.6% of those (39/49) self-reported using colour; 57.6% (57/99) reported colour use overall. Networks: 46/99 (46.5%). Mean delay 130 +/- 95 trials in humans vs 175 +/- 105 in networks (p=0.04). No insight-like networks at zero update noise, 100% above noise of about 0.05. L2 or no regularisation gave no insight-like pattern.
limits: One task type. Models behaviour, not experience. Supports the view that suddenness can come from gradual learning.
agent_relevance: Sudden behaviour does not prove a separate restructuring mechanism. It can be silent knowledge crossing a gate threshold, so a probe or check that opens the gate may beat a new search.

source: Cross-paper synthesis: three uses of 'aha' in 2025-2026 LLM work
finding: 'Aha' is used as a training outcome (R1-Zero), as a prompted behaviour, and as a measured accuracy gain at a pivot. Only the third has been tested, and it mostly fails.
numbers: From files opened here: formal Aha 1.79% of samples (Illusion of Insight); 8.3% of VLM responses (Aha Revisited); no positive link to accuracy in R1-Zero (Liu et al.); pseudo-aha causes 77-100% of errors on EvolMath.
limits: Synthesis across different models and tasks, not one study.
agent_relevance: Define restructuring in the schema by what changes (frame, constraint, representation) and test the gain. Do not rely on the word aha.

source: Coverage gap: classic insight paradigms on current LLMs
finding: No paper was found that runs Duncker's candle problem, the nine-dot problem or matchstick problems on 2024-2026 LLMs with human norms. The field uses riddles, lateral puzzles and rebuses as proxies.
numbers: Searches this session: an arXiv listing for 'insight problems', 'functional fixedness', 'nine-dot' and Duncker returned no matching papers. The web-search budget ran out, so coverage is incomplete.
limits: Absence of evidence from a limited search. A psychology-journal paper outside arXiv may exist.
agent_relevance: Treat classic-paradigm LLM results as unmeasured. Do not assume models pass or fail them.
